D4a-03 closing; stage D4 done. 35 branches (F01 to F35) and 759 cross-links; 476 rooms in a branch, 229 in none; the comparison (chunk-comparison-v1.1, a declared departure) carries k 4 (silhouette 0.024) and k 2 without the low-information rows, does not survive a change of distance, and largely sorts rooms by size (eta squared 0.255); the projections' canvas percentiles follow size. Working hypothesis: the rooms adapted the model in many small shared ways at once, so the branches are facets, not forms; the families across elements (the shared instruction kept current, help conditional, carrying on renewed, P05's clause limited where informed members reject a change) are the next stage's material, read within size. D4a-04 opened (25 October), an extra D4 leg on J's instruction (25 Oct 21:39 Berlin, through the handler): can the 25 top-level branches be joined into fewer parents on grounds the stage and contract allow? Decide from the record; if a join is defensible, make it as D4 cuts and say how D5 is organized (one leg per parent); if not, say why in notes-D4.md and change nothing (D5 one leg per branch). J will not be asked again. Read AGENT.md, the head, STAGE-D4 (unchanged), diary --last 5, validate --open D4 (the same literal-pattern error). The test, written before any computation: a parent must be a branch the stage allows. (1) It is grounded on keys its members all hold at its level (section 2; the material never stands alone). (2) A subform nests by adding keys, and stage_D4.py accepts a child only if each parent key has the same op and target as a child key and the child's node lifts to the parent's node; so a parent can join only branches of one element and one op. (3) A group that meets only at the dimension or the bare target is a grouping, not a branch (section 2; cut rule R4). (4) No list of rooms that belong together may come from anywhere but the ledger, so co-membership alone grounds no parent. The handler's two facts are checked by script, not adopted.

The join check (out/_analysis/d4a04_joins.py, its output d4a04_joins.txt). The handler's facts, checked: 25 top-level branches on 14 elements; by the elements' own dimension field D02 9, D07 5, D03 4, D04 4, D06 2, D01 1, as the handler says, but by the dimension each branch's key lifts to D02 9, D04 6, D07 6, D06 2, D01 1, D03 1 (F07 lifts to D02, F26 to D04, F32 to D07), and the ladder joins by the key's lift, not the element's field. Jaccard distance between member sets: median 0.977, minimum 0.870 (F10 and F26); average linkage first merges at 0.870, not above 0.89 as the handler says; at 0.95 it gives 13 groups, six of them joining branches of different elements. Joins the stage allows: a parent needs keys every member holds, and stage_D4.py nests a child only under a key of the same op and target. Only three sets share element and op. P04 add-step (F15, F33) meet first at the dimension, add-step:P04:D02, 85 rooms, 20 in neither child. P16 add-condition (F22, F28) meet at the dimension, add-condition:P16:D04, 65 rooms, 13 in neither child. P05 restrict (F07, F26, F27) meet only at the bare target, restrict:P05:*, 214 rooms, 106 in none of them. Each is a grouping under section 2 and cut rule R4, and each would bring in rooms whose lines were never read for the shared change (R2). The families that span ops or elements (P05's clause and the marking; the shared instruction; carrying on; the chat; machine hands; the frame; help) have no common key, and rooms in all of their branches number 0 to 5, so no parent can be grounded on keys, and co-membership alone may not ground one. Decision: no join is defensible; nothing changes; D5 runs as the stage says, one leg per branch.

D4a-05 opened, an extra D4 leg after D5 closed, on J's instruction through the handler. Oriented: AGENT.md, head, STAGE-D4, diary --last 5, validate --open D4 (one 'missing' error: the literal name _views/rooms-x-adaptations.<level>.<kind>.tsv). Dated amendment recorded before any computation (departures.jsonl line 11), under J's ruling of 7 October, quoting J, 26 October 2026, 17:27 Berlin: 'I need to tell it to make something with 4 to 8 big forms and then continue clustering down to 700.' J, 18:01 Berlin: stage D6 builds on these 4 to 8 forms, with the 35 branches as the level below. It applies forward only: the room tree is added above the 35 branches; no branch, key, member, cross-link, D5 account or the model changes. Selected changes, defined from the ledger before clustering (out/_analysis/d4a05_explore.py, read before this line): the shared lines (adaptation_ledger.shared_lines) whose op changes the model (restrict 2,994, add-step 1,421, add-condition 1,223, link 996, contradict 3), on elements and arrows alike; 21 rooms hold none, the core the instruction names.

D4a-05 method for the room tree, written before any clustering (facts from out/_analysis/d4a05_facts.py, read before this line: 6,637 selected change lines, 2,126 on arrows, 3 without a lift and so unplaceable; 684 rooms with changes, 1 to 26 each, median 9; third-order nodes 171, of which 23 are held by one room, 34 lines; fourth-order 29 nodes; 9 dimensions). (1) Unit: the room. Each selected line counts once at its third-order node, its fourth-order node and its dimension, from its lift; arrows count through the third-order theme of their source, as elements do; op and element are not features. (2) Changes made by one room: the 23 third-order nodes held by one room are dropped at the third-order level only. (3) Mix, not number: each room's counts become shares within each level. (4) Distance: Hellinger at each level; the three levels count equally (squared distances averaged), embedded as square-root shares so Ward's method applies. (5) Top: Ward on the 684 rooms with changes; for k = 4 to 8, the silhouette, the sizes and their largest-to-smallest ratio, bootstrap stability (100 resamples, seed 0, adjusted Rand) and a column-permutation null (20 copies, seed 1). The k carried is the one with the highest silhouette, if its bootstrap stability is 0.5 or more; else the most stable k. (6) A form is reported as broad, and not kept as a form, if no fourth-order node is over-represented in it (1.5 times the population share, in at least a third of its members) and its members are set apart only by more changes or a more even spread; then its rooms go to their nearest other form and the cut is reread. (7) Below each form: Ward bisection, kept as a level only if both halves hold 5 rooms or more (the stage's minimum group size) and the split's between-group share of the sum of squares beats the 95th percentile of 99 column permutations within the node (seed 2); recursion stops where a split fails, and the full dendrogram below runs on to the rooms. (8) Each room appears once, in its Ward form; its other forms, listed as secondary, are those whose signature fourth-order nodes hold 25 per cent or more of its selected changes; a room fits two forms equally well if its second-nearest form centroid is within 5 per cent of its own. (9) The 21 rooms with no selected change are the core, kept together. (10) The 35 branches: each room's primary branch is the one whose key holds most of its lines, the others secondary; each branch is placed under the form holding most of its members, with the spread reported. (11) Afterwards, the forms are read against the rooms' codes (fourth-order composition of first-order concepts, which the tree does not use): a permutation test of form labels on the code compositions, nearest-centroid agreement against chance, and the median coded concepts per form for size. Sensitivity: average linkage on the mean Hellinger distance, and the single-room nodes kept.
